# From IG Ranking to a Biological Narrative

## 1. What the evidence actually shows

**The attribution is broad and shallow, not pathway-dominated.** Scores decay smoothly from 0.076 (PTMA) to 0.009 (MGP) — only ~8-fold across all 500 features — and the median is ~0.015. Even the top 50 features are only ~2–5× the median. No single receptor, kinase, or transcription factor dominates; the model reads Ki-67 off a *distributed cellular state*. The only feature that clearly separates from the continuum is PTMA (#1, ~1.3× the #2 feature, ~5× the median).

**The top of the list is a coherent "cell-growth" program**, not a random collection:

- **Ribosome biogenesis & protein synthesis (~⅓ of the top 100):** PABPC1 (#2), RPLP0 (#6), RPS18 (#8), RPS27/RPS3A/RPS7 (#13–15), RPL41/RPL34/RPL39 (#25–29), RPS29, RPLP1, RPL21, RPS11, RPL7A, RPS13, RPL36, RPL30, RPS21, RPS24 (18 ribosomal proteins in the top 100), plus EIF5A, EIF1, EIF4H, NOP56 (#21, box C/D snoRNP for rRNA 2′-O-methylation), NCL/nucleolin (#84), CNBP, PTMS (#34), ERH, and hnRNP/spliceosome genes.
- **Anabolic & energy metabolism:** ALDOA (#12), PKM (#28), TPI1, ENO1, LDHA (glycolysis); TALDO1, PGD, TKT (pentose phosphate — ribose/NADPH for nucleotide synthesis); GLUL (#16), ASS1 (#30), MAT2A, PHGDH (nitrogen, SAM, serine); FTH1 (#4, iron — required for ribonucleotide reductase and mitochondrial enzymes); NAMPT (NAD salvage); FABP7 (#7), FASN, SREBF1 (lipids); a large OXPHOS block (COX8A #20, NDUFS5, COX5B, NDUFS2, SDHA, ATP5ME/MF…).
- **Mitotic machinery:** TUBB4B (#9), TUBA1C (#11), TUBB, ANLN, MAPRE1, MYL6/MYH9/MYL12B, CKS2 (#3, CDK1/2 regulatory subunit), CDK2AP1 (#39), BUB3, CKS1B, CDK1, MYBL2, STMN1, TK1, NME1/2, SPC24.
- **Chromatin/growth antigens:** PTMA (#1) and PTMS (#34) — both acidic nuclear proteins with histone-chaperone-like activity; H2AX (#53); HMGN1, HMGB2, HMGA1.
- **Breast-tumor context:** AR (#55), ZNF703 (#67, luminal-B 8p12 amplicon driver), HDGF (#5), MDK (#72), ASPH (#56), MUCL1 (#17), WFDC2, AZGP1, KRT8/7/19/18, EPCAM, CD24, XBP1, SPDEF, ESRP1, PIP.
- **Replication-stress/DNA-damage markers at mid-high rank:** H2AX (#53), PRKDC (#63), XRCC5, RAD23A/B.

**What is *not* high is equally informative:** canonical cell-cycle execution genes are mid-to-low (CDK1 #234, MYBL2 #335, STMN1 #385, TK1 #405, HMGA1 #476, SPC24 #479), and replication-dependent histone genes cluster almost entirely in the bottom fifth (ranks ~440–500; H2AX is the exception). ESR1, ERBB2, and MAPK-pathway genes are absent from the panel entirely, so receptor/MAPK signaling cannot be the basis of the prediction. SERHL2 (#10) is functionally poorly characterized — I cannot interpret it and will not pretend otherwise.

## 2. Single best hypothesis

**Ki-67 abundance in these breast cancer cells is a quantitative readout of the coordinated cell-growth program — nucleolar ribosome biogenesis + protein synthesis + supporting anabolic/energy metabolism + mitotic readiness — rather than the output of any single oncogenic pathway.** Mechanistically, Ki-67 is co-induced with (and itself functions within) this same nucleolar program: Ki-67 is a nucleolar/perichromosomal protein implicated in rRNA metabolism and mitotic chromosome organization, so the ribosome/translation module is the strongest single-cell predictor of the Ki-67-high state. The leading individual features fit: PTMA is a classic Myc-responsive, proliferation-associated chromatin chaperone; CKS2 is a CDK1/2 accessory subunit overexpressed in proliferating tumors; HDGF and MDK are mitogens reported to mark poor prognosis in breast carcinoma; FABP7 is linked to aggressive, proliferative breast cancer phenotypes.

## 3. Established knowledge vs. new testable claim

**(a) Mostly confirms established literature:** Ki-67 marks cycling cells (Gerdes et al., Int J Cancer 1983; J Immunol 1984; Scholzen & Gerdes, J Cell Physiol 2000); Ki-67 is functionally required for proliferation and organizes mitotic chromosomes/perichromosomal layer (e.g., Rahmanzadeh et al., 2007; Sobecki et al., 2016; Cuylen-Haering et al., Nature 2020; reviewed in Sun & Kaufman, Chromosoma 2018); ribosome biogenesis is rate-limiting for and coupled to cancer proliferation (Ruggero & Pandolfi, Nat Rev Cancer 2003; Montanaro et al., Am J Pathol 2008; Derenzini et al., J Pathol 2000); proliferating cells reprogram glycolysis/PPP/serine metabolism (Vander Heiden et al., Science 2009; Possemato et al., Nature 2011). *Caveat: citations are from memory and should be verified.*

**(b) The new, testable refinement:** in this in-situ breast cancer setting, the growth/translation module *out-ranks* canonical cell-cycle and histone genes as the basis for Ki-67 prediction. This predicts that Ki-67 tracks nucleolar/biosynthetic output (cell growth) more tightly than cell-cycle phase per se.

**Concrete predictions:** (1) In independent breast cancer scRNA/spatial data, MKI67 will correlate more strongly with a ribosome/translation module score (RPL/RPS + EIFs + PABPC1 + NOP56 + NCL) than with S-phase/histone module scores, and partial-correlating out the ribosome module will strongly attenuate the cell-cycle module's association. (2) Pol I inhibition (CX-5461/low-dose actinomycin D) or mTORC1 inhibition in breast cancer lines will reduce Ki-67 protein before complete cycle arrest; PTMA or CKS2 knockdown will reduce Ki-67 and proliferation. (3) Spatially, Ki-67-high cells will occupy niches co-enriched for ribosomal/metabolic transcripts (plausibly in AR/ZNF703/XBP1-high luminal-B regions).

## 4. What I cannot determine from this evidence (honesty section)

- **No direction of effect:** only |IG| is given. Whether PTMA, ribosomal genes, etc., positively or negatively predict Ki-67 is *not* in the data; my sign assignments come from literature, not the ranking.
- **Averaging confound:** mean |IG| over all cells systematically favors features elevated in *all* cycling cells (ribosomal/growth genes) over phase-specific genes (histones, mitotic genes). The "growth > cycle-phase" conclusion is therefore partly confounded by the aggregation method. The histone result is also technically suspect (non-polyadenylated, short-lived transcripts; conversely, highly expressed ribosomal mRNAs can attract larger IG magnitudes simply from scale).
- **IG-ONLY ablation:** with no classifier, I cannot verify that the top features are *sufficient* to separate Ki-67-high from Ki-67-low cells, whether the signal comes from one subgroup (e.g., FABP7-high vs. AR-high niches), or whether the upstream model predicts Ki-67 well at all — if it predicts poorly, this ranking is noise. Per-cell attributions, effect directions, and subgroup statistics would be needed to firm this up.
